dm: Even if he should acquire some gain, If he is working for me, I shall give him only enough for his livelihood, And I shall take the rest by my own power.
gm: Even if this one has wealth, If he does my work, Having given him just enough to live on, I will take it by my power.

dm: I shall cause his happiness to decline, And I shall constantly subject him to harm; For throughout hundreds of lifetimes, He has caused me harm within saṃsāra.
gm: This one shall be made to fall from happiness, and Be constantly subjected to my harm. In all hundreds of ways, This one has harmed me in saṃsāra.

dm: O mind, though countless eons have passed while you desired to pursue your own interests, Through such great hardship, You have achieved nothing but suffering.
gm: O mind, because you desired to accomplish your own purpose, Even though countless eons have passed, With such great weariness, You have accomplished only suffering.

dm: Therefore, you must certainly and thoroughly apply yourself to the welfare of others; Since the Buddha's word is unerring, You will later see the benefits of this.
gm: Thus, you must certainly Fully engage in the purpose of others. Since the words of the Muni are infallible, You will see its good qualities later.

dm: If you had performed this work in the past, It would be impossible for you to be in this present state, Lacking the perfect bliss of a Buddha.
gm: If in former times You had performed this action, A state other than the perfect happiness of a Buddha, Such a situation as this could not possibly occur.

dm: Therefore, just as you have grasped as "I" these drops of others' semen and blood, You should likewise habituate yourself to regarding others in the same way.
gm: Therefore, just as Upon the drops of semen and blood of others, You have grasped as "I", Likewise make it a habit with others too.

dm: Having formed the great conception of "other," Seize whatever appears as your own body, And take that very thing away, To use it for the benefit of others.
gm: Having become a great spy for others, Whatever appears on my body, Having stolen those very things, You should practice what is beneficial for others.

dm: "I am happy, but others are not; I am high, but others are low; I am the benefactor, but others are not"— Why do you not feel envy toward yourself in this way?
gm: "I am happy, others are unhappy, I am high, others are low, I do what is beneficial, others do not." Why do you not feel jealous of yourself?

dm: Separate yourself from your own happiness, And take the sufferings of others upon yourself. At all times, examine your own faults, Asking, "What is this [self] doing?"
gm: Separate yourself from happiness, and Apply the suffering of others to yourself. Thinking, "What is this one doing at any time?" Examine your own faults.

dm: Even when others commit a wrong, Transform it into your own fault; And though your own mistake be small, Confess it openly to many people.
gm: Even when faults have been committed by others, Transform them into your own faults; And even if a fault committed by yourself is small, Confess it fully to many people.

dm: By speaking highly of the renown of others, Let your own reputation be eclipsed. Like the lowliest of servants, Employ yourself in all matters of benefit.
gm: By exalting the reputation of others, Suppress your own reputation. Like the lowest of servants, Employ yourself for all purposes.

dm: This [self] is faulty by nature, So do not praise it for any fleeting qualities. Act in such a way that no one at all Will ever know of its virtues.
gm: This one is of a faulty nature, Do not praise it for its adventitious good qualities. By all means, regarding its good qualities, Act so that no one at all will know them.

dm: In short, whatever harm you have done To others for your own sake, Let that harm fall upon yourself For the sake of sentient beings.
gm: In short, for the sake of your own purpose, Whatever harm you have done to others, For the sake of the purpose of sentient beings, Let that harm descend upon yourself.

dm: Do not allow it to grow strong In an overbearing and arrogant manner; Like a new bride, Remain bashful, fearful, and restrained.
gm: Lest it become domineering, Do not foster its strength. Just like a new bride, Keep it bound by modesty and fear.

dm: That should be done, and one should remain so; You must not act in that way. In this manner, you must be brought under control; If you transgress this, you shall be suppressed.
gm: "Do that! Remain like that! You must not do like that!" In this way, subjugate it, And if it transgresses that, it must be punished.

dm: However, if you, my mind, do not act accordingly Even when you have been so instructed, Then, since all faults reside in you, You shall simply be suppressed.
gm: However, even if instructed like that, O mind, if you do not do so, Since all faults rely upon you, You yourself will just have to be punished.

dm: The former time when you could ruin me Was another matter; Now that I see you, where can you go? I shall crush all of your pride.
gm: The former times when you ruined me Were a different time; Now I see you, where will you go? I shall destroy all your arrogance.

dm: Furthermore, abandon the thought that you still have your own interests; I have sold you to others. Do not be distressed, but offer up your service.
gm: "I still have my own purpose"— Cast away that thought which thinks it exists! Since I have sold you to others, Do not feel sorrow, offer your services.

dm: If, through heedlessness, you do not give yourself to sentient beings, You will certainly hand me over to the guardians of hell.
gm: If, becoming careless, I do not give you to sentient beings, You will surely hand me over To the guards of hell.

dm: By handing me over in that way, you have caused me to suffer for a long time; Now, remembering those grudges, I shall destroy your self-interested thoughts.
gm: In that way, you have indeed Handed me over, and I have suffered for a long time; Remembering those grudges, I shall destroy your thinking of your own purpose.

dm: Therefore, if I desire to be happy, I should not seek my own pleasure. Therefore, if I desire to protect myself, I should constantly protect others.
gm: Therefore, if I wish to be happy, I must not make myself happy. Therefore, if I wish to protect myself, I must always protect others.

dm: To whatever extent this body is pampered and cared for, To that same extent it falls into a state of extreme fragility.
gm: To whatever extent this body Is thoroughly cared for, To that very extent, it falls into Becoming extremely fragile.

dm: For one who has fallen into such a state, Even this entire earth is unable to satisfy their desires; Who then can fulfill such cravings?
gm: And even for that which has fallen in that way, Its desires, even by this entire earth, Cannot be fulfilled; So who is able to fulfill its desires?

dm: When one desires the impossible, afflictions and a shattered peace of mind will arise; However, for one who is independent of all such things, their excellence is inexhaustible.
gm: Desiring the impossible brings afflictions, And disappointed hopes will also arise. But for one who does not depend on anything, Their excellence knows no exhaustion.

dm: Therefore, one should not provide any opportunity for the desires of the body to increase; Whatever one does not grasp as attractive is the finest of things.
gm: Therefore, for the desires of the body, One should not give the opportunity to increase. Not grasping at whatever is pleasant— That is an excellent thing.

dm: Ultimately ending in ashes, it is inert and moved by others; Why do I grasp this unbearable, impure form as a self?
gm: Ultimately ending in ashes, Motionless, to be moved by others, An unbearable, impure form— Why do I grasp at this as 'I'?

dm: Whether it is alive or even if it is dead, What use is this machine to me? If it is no different from a clod of earth or the like, Alas, why do I not dispel my pride?
gm: Whether it is alive or whether it is dead, What use is this machine to me? If there is no difference between this and a clod of earth, Alas, why do I not dispel my pride?

dm: By following the dictates of the body, I have accumulated meaningless suffering; What is the use of attachment or anger Toward this thing that is just like a piece of wood?
gm: By taking care of the body, Having accumulated meaningless suffering, Attachment and anger— What use are they for this thing similar to wood?

dm: Whether I nurture it in this way, Or it is eaten by vultures and the like, Since it has neither attachment nor hatred, Why then do I feel attachment for it?
gm: Whether it is cared for by me in this way, Or whether it is eaten by vultures and the like, Since it has no attachment and no anger, Why do I become attached to it?

dm: If that which is angered by insults And that which is pleased by praise Is itself without consciousness, For whose sake do I exert myself?
gm: That which is angered by blame, And that which is delighted by praise— If it itself lacks any knowing, For whose sake have I toiled?

dm: If you say that those who desire this body Are my friends, Since everyone desires their own body, Why do I not take pleasure in them as well?
gm: Whoever desires this body, If I think, 'They and I are friends,' Since everyone desires their own body, Why do I not rejoice in them?

dm: Therefore, without attachment, I shall give up this body for the benefit of all beings; Thus, although it has many faults, I shall maintain it as a tool for my actions.
gm: Therefore, without attachment, I shall give up my body to benefit beings. Thus, even though it has many faults, It should be retained as an instrument for action.

dm: Therefore, enough of childish behavior! Following in the footsteps of the wise, And recalling the instructions on conscientiousness, I shall dispel sleep and mental dullness.
gm: Therefore, enough with childish behavior! I shall follow in the footsteps of the wise, And, remembering the teachings on conscientiousness, I shall turn away from sleep and lethargy.

dm: Therefore, in order to clear away obscurations, I shall withdraw my mind from mistaken paths, And always rest it in meditative equipoise Upon the perfect object of focus.
gm: Therefore, in order to clear away obscurations, Having withdrawn the mind from wrong paths, Constantly upon the perfect object, I shall rest in meditative equipoise.

dm: This concludes the eighth chapter, titled "The Explanation of Meditative Concentration," from the *Entering the Conduct of a Bodhisattva*.
gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the eighth chapter, called The Teaching on Meditative Concentration.
